ops.title: installedApplicationPath resolves the app root from $HOME while daemonkit resolves agents from the passwd DB — Homebrew's canonical temp home turned the mismatch from loud to silent
ops.description:
captain-hook resolves the installed app root from the caller's environment while daemonkit resolves LaunchAgent and state paths from the passwd database. Under any caller with a remapped HOME the two halves converge DIFFERENT MACHINES: the bundle lands in the fake home, the agents are written to the real one.

internal/hookd/deployment.go:56-64

    func installedApplicationPath() (string, error) {
        home, err := os.UserHomeDir()          // <- $HOME
        ...
        resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home)
        if err != nil || resolved != home {
            return "", errors.New("captain package: user home must be a canonical real directory")
        }

against daemonkit/paths/paths.go and daemonkit/launchd/agent.go:156, which resolve "the home resolved through the passwd database so a sandboxed caller HOME" cannot relocate state — a deliberate daemonkit invariant that captain-hook's app-path half does not honor.

WHY THIS IS NOT A RESTATEMENT OF 0ef22da2. That bug is the sandbox write-denial: post_install cannot write ~/Library/LaunchAgents, full stop. This one is the reason the failure stopped being visible. Its severity changed on 2026-08-07 without a captain-hook commit.

Homebrew remaps HOME for post_install (/opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/formula.rb:1668):

    # Formula post-install creates its isolated HOME inside the child because
    # the entire `postinstall.rb` process is already sandboxed by its parent.
    Dir.mktmpdir("#{name}-postinstall-", HOMEBREW_TEMP) do |home|

Homebrew commit f8fcbd88e0 (2026-08-07, "Sandbox structured cask operations") added the HOMEBREW_TEMP argument. Before it, the temp home came from the ambient TMPDIR (/var/folders/...), which is NOT canonical (/var -> /private/var), so EvalSymlinks tripped the guard above and post_install failed loudly at the guard. After it, HOMEBREW_TEMP is /private/tmp, the fake home IS canonical, the guard passes, and the deploy silently lands in a throwaway directory that Dir.mktmpdir then deletes.

EVIDENCE (yasyf-box, 2026-08-29, captain-hook 12.22.4 / daemonkit v0.23.0 / Homebrew 6.0.20-54):

1. The post_install log reports failure at ACTIVATE, not at land:
     captain package: activate installed app: deploy: apply agent "com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper": ...
     open /Users/yasyf/Library/LaunchAgents/.com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper.plist.545221131: operation not permitted
   That message is only reachable after land() returns nil (internal/hookd/deployment.go:180-232).

2. Yet the real bundle was untouched. ~/Applications/Captain Hook.app still had inode 403466244 — exactly the file_id.inode recorded in the Aug-16 activation.json — and ~/Applications/.daemonkit-deploy/Captain Hook/ had mtime 2026-08-16 14:16:50, i.e. no Aug-29 writes at all.

3. A Supersede against the real path must either replace those bytes or fail. It did neither.

4. The same verb run unsandboxed with the real HOME immediately reached the real bundle, refusing with paths under /Users/yasyf/Applications/Captain Hook.app/Contents/Helpers/capt-hookd — the control that isolates HOME as the variable.

EXPLICITLY MARKED AS INFERENCE: points 1-4 are direct observations. The causal attribution to Homebrew f8fcbd88e0 — that the guard used to fire and stopped — is an inference forced by that evidence plus the two Homebrew source lines, NOT something observed by running the pre-f8fcbd88e0 Homebrew. It is the only reading consistent with a successful land that wrote nothing to the real home, but it has not been reproduced against the older Homebrew and should not be recorded as though it had been.

FIX: resolve the app root through daemonkit's passwd-derived paths, the same source the agents already use. A HOME-derived app path and a passwd-derived agent path should not be independently derivable — one home resolution, or the halves can disagree again the next time a packaging tool remaps the environment. Note that this fix alone does NOT make brew delivery work; 0ef22da2's sandbox write-denial still blocks that. What it buys is that the failure is loud and names the right machine.

ops.text: installedApplicationPath() resolves the app root through daemonkit's passwd-derived paths, so the app path and the LaunchAgent path cannot name different homes
A package-install run under a remapped HOME either converges the real machine or fails loudly; it never silently deploys into the remapped home

A regression test runs package-install with HOME set to a canonical directory other than the passwd home and asserts the deploy targets the passwd home (the pre-f8fcbd88e0 non-canonical case must not be the only one covered)
